To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the survival rate of patients with transitional cell carcinoma of bladder (TCC) having tumours with diploid chromosomal number of cells was significantly higher than the survival rate of those with tumours with hyperdiploid number.
cytogenetic analysis of transitional cell carcinoma of bladder can predict the clinical behaviour of tumours and can be used to select patients for more aggressive treatment.
the modal chromosome count is the most important factor predicting progression-free survival and that the category of the tumour is the most important in predicting survival.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new method for the prediction of the biological behaviour of TCC of the urinary bladder.
the potential use of numerical abnormalities of chromosomes as a prognostic factor in patients with bladder carcinoma.
the cytogenetic analysis in bladder tumours.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cytogenetic analysis of TCC is useful in predicting the survival of patients with superficial tumour and the progression-free survival in tumours of all stages.
the chromosomal modal number is a valuable tool for the prediction of progression-free survival and survival in patients with bladder carcinoma.
a high number of hyperdiploid chromosomes is a significant adverse prognostic factor, especially for patients with superficial tumour.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the modal chromosome numbers of TCCs were useful in predicting survival and progression-free intervals in TCCs of all categories, but particularly so in superficial tumours.
the modal chromosome numbers of the bladder tumours are useful in predicting the clinical behaviour of TCC, especially in patients with superficial bladder tumours.
the cytogenetic analysis of transitional cell carcinoma of bladder is a useful tool in determining the prognosis for patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the number of chromosomes is a very good prognostic factor in bladder cancer, and that the more chromosomes the patient has, the worse the prognosis.
the chromosomal status of the tumour is a useful tool to predict the clinical behaviour of the disease.
cytogenetic analysis can provide important information for the prognosis and treatment of TCC patients.
